words.enDefinition: a person who owns a business and takes part in running its daily operations

examples.en: As the owner-operator, Leila set the schedule and worked the counter on busy afternoons.
examples.zh: 莉拉是「亲自经营的业主」，她排班，也在客流大的下午照看柜台。

examples.en: I asked the owner-operator how she balanced repairs and sales with her afternoon classes.
examples.zh: 我问那位「亲自经营的业主」，她如何兼顾维修、销售和下午的课。

words.enDefinition: a plan for how many workers a business needs, with what skills and at which times

examples.en: The staffing plan put an experienced worker on the stall for each busy lunch period.
examples.zh: 「人员配置计划」在每个繁忙的午餐时段都安排了一名有经验的员工值摊。

examples.en: Our team revised the staffing plan after learning when the evening classes would finish.
examples.zh: 知道晚课几点结束后，我们团队修改了「人员配置计划」。

words.enDefinition: the number of staff working or available in an organisation or during a particular period

examples.en: The manager increased the staffing level when the campus fair moved to the larger hall.
examples.zh: 校园展会移到更大的大厅后，经理调高了「人员配备水平」。

examples.en: We maintained the same staffing level even when half the stalls closed for lunch.
examples.zh: 即使一半摊位午餐时暂停营业，我们仍维持同样的「人员配备水平」。

words.enDefinition: a time or role for which there are fewer workers available than needed

examples.en: The rota revealed a staffing gap just before the evening concert was due to begin.
examples.zh: 排班表显示，晚间音乐会即将开场时会出现「人员缺口」。

examples.en: We covered the staffing gap by moving one worker from packing to the counter.
examples.zh: 我们把一名员工从打包岗位调到柜台，补上了「人员缺口」。

words.enDefinition: the smallest number of people required to carry out a specified operation or task

examples.en: We agreed the minimum crew size for opening the studio would be two people.
examples.zh: 我们商定，开放工作室的「最低班组人数」是两人。

examples.en: The supervisor checked the minimum crew size before approving the quietest shift of the week.
examples.zh: 主管批准一周最清闲的班次前，核对了「最低班组人数」。

words.enDefinition: a time during which demand for a product or service is especially high

examples.en: The lunch hour was our peak-demand period because most students finished class at noon.
examples.zh: 午餐时间是我们的「需求高峰时段」，因为大多数学生中午才下课。

examples.en: We stocked the counter before the peak-demand period began at the end of lectures.
examples.zh: 课程结束后就是「需求高峰时段」，我们提前给柜台补好了货。

words.enDefinition: a work shift scheduled for a period when demand is comparatively low

examples.en: I took an off-peak shift on Wednesday to learn how to count the stock.
examples.zh: 我周三上了一个「非高峰班次」，学习怎么清点库存。

examples.en: The new volunteer chose an off-peak shift because it was easier to ask questions then.
examples.zh: 新志愿者选了「非高峰班次」，那时比较方便提问。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of how many workers will be needed in future periods

examples.en: Our staffing forecast used last year's visitor counts for each afternoon of the student fair.
examples.zh: 我们的「人员需求预测」参考了去年学生展会每天下午的来访人数。

examples.en: The coordinator updated the staffing forecast when a large club booked the evening slot.
examples.zh: 一个大型社团订了晚间时段后，协调员更新了「人员需求预测」。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of the amount of work expected during a future period

examples.en: We based the workload forecast on how many orders had arrived before each previous event.
examples.zh: 我们用之前每场活动前收到的订单数来做「工作量预测」。

examples.en: The workload forecast showed that Thursday would be busier than the rest of the week.
examples.zh: 「工作量预测」显示，周四会比这周其他日子忙。

words.enDefinition: a planned limit on the number of positions or workers that can be supported

examples.en: The student enterprise set a headcount budget before deciding how many extra people to hire.
examples.zh: 学生企业先定了「人员编制预算」，再决定多招多少人。

examples.en: We checked whether the headcount budget allowed another weekend position for the summer term.
examples.zh: 我们查了「人员编制预算」能否在夏季学期再安排一个周末岗位。

words.enDefinition: operating with fewer workers than are needed to handle the work comfortably

examples.en: The stall was short-staffed after two workers discovered they had exams on the same afternoon.
examples.zh: 两名员工发现当天下午都有考试，摊位那一班便「人手不足」。

examples.en: We stayed open while short-staffed, but we stopped taking repair bookings for the evening.
examples.zh: 「人手不足」时我们继续营业，不过暂停接晚间维修预约。

words.enDefinition: having all the workers needed or planned for a shift, team or location

examples.en: The desk was fully staffed by noon, just as the first group of visitors arrived.
examples.zh: 到中午，服务台「人员配齐」，正赶上第一批来访者到场。

examples.en: We expect the evening stall to be fully staffed once the new volunteers finish training.
examples.zh: 我们预计新志愿者培训结束后，晚间摊位就能「人员配齐」。

collocations: make sure the desk is fully staffed

words.enDefinition: having more workers available than the amount of work reasonably requires

examples.en: The stall seemed overstaffed on Friday because most students left after their last lecture.
examples.zh: 周五大多数学生上完最后一堂课就走了，摊位看起来「人员配备过多」。

examples.en: We try to avoid being overstaffed in the morning when deliveries have not yet arrived.
examples.zh: 早上货物还没送到，我们尽量避免「人员配备过多」。

words.enDefinition: the supervisor responsible for a workplace or activity during the current shift

examples.en: The on-duty supervisor helped a new cashier check the register before the first sale.
examples.zh: 第一笔销售前，「在岗主管」帮新收银员检查了收银机。

examples.en: I left a message for the on-duty supervisor about the spare keys in the office.
examples.zh: 我给「在岗主管」留了条消息，说备用钥匙放在办公室。

words.enDefinition: a person who coordinates workers and tasks during a particular shift

examples.en: The shift lead assigned one person to the counter and another to the collection shelf.
examples.zh: 「值班组长」安排一人管柜台，另一人管自取货架。

examples.en: I asked the shift lead which jobs still needed doing before the evening handover.
examples.zh: 我问「值班组长」，晚班交接前还有什么工作要做。

words.enDefinition: a manager responsible for overseeing a business or location during a particular period

examples.en: The duty manager moved two employees to the entrance when the queue reached the stairs.
examples.zh: 队伍排到了楼梯口，「值班经理」便调了两名员工到入口。

examples.en: We contacted the duty manager before changing the opening time on the noticeboard outside.
examples.zh: 我们先联系了「值班经理」，才修改室外公告栏上的开门时间。

words.enDefinition: one of the people who work together as a crew to carry out a job

examples.en: Each crew member checked one section of the hall after the last visitor had gone.
examples.zh: 最后一位访客离开后，每名「班组成员」检查了大厅的一个区域。

examples.en: I showed a new crew member where we kept the supplies for the next shift.
examples.zh: 我给新来的「班组成员」指出了下一班用的物资放在哪里。

words.enDefinition: staff engaged to work as needed, often without a regular schedule

examples.en: We brought in casual staff for the fair because Friday would be especially busy.
examples.zh: 周五展会特别忙，我们为此安排了「按需排班的员工」。

examples.en: The rota listed casual staff separately so the coordinator could confirm their available hours.
examples.zh: 排班表单列了「按需排班的员工」，方便协调员确认他们有空的时段。

words.enDefinition: a short-term arrangement in which someone takes over work while the usual worker is unavailable

examples.en: The shop arranged temporary cover while the regular supervisor attended a conference off campus.
examples.zh: 常驻主管去校外开会时，店里做了「临时替岗安排」。

examples.en: We found temporary cover for the equipment desk during the busy part of the afternoon.
examples.zh: 下午最忙的那个时段，我们给器材服务台做了「临时替岗安排」。

collocations: find temporary cover for a shift

words.enDefinition: a person assigned to take over another worker's duties for a short period

examples.en: A relief worker ran the counter while the usual cashier trained two new volunteers.
examples.zh: 原来的收银员去培训两名新志愿者时，一名「替班人员」接管了柜台。

examples.en: The relief worker checked the handover notes before serving the first customer of the evening.
examples.zh: 「替班人员」先看了交接记录，再接待晚上的第一位顾客。

words.enDefinition: workers assigned wherever they are needed rather than to a single fixed station

examples.en: The floating staff helped with packing until more customers arrived at the pickup desk.
examples.zh: 「机动人员」先帮忙打包，等到自取台顾客多了再过去帮忙。

examples.en: We kept two floating staff free to help wherever the queue began to grow.
examples.zh: 我们留了两名「机动人员」，哪边排队的人开始多了就去哪边帮忙。

words.enDefinition: workers who are available to respond or come in if called during an agreed period

examples.en: The coordinator arranged for on-call staff to handle deliveries arriving after the afternoon shift.
examples.zh: 协调员安排了「随时待命的员工」，处理下午班结束后到的送货。

examples.en: The on-call staff were contacted only when the queue could no longer be managed safely.
examples.zh: 排队的人多到难以维持秩序时，团队才联系了「随时待命的员工」。

collocations: make sure on-call staff are available

words.enDefinition: the workers responsible for getting a workplace ready at the start of the day

examples.en: The opening crew checked the displays and put the signs out before the market opened.
examples.zh: 「开店班组」先检查陈列并把指示牌放到外面，然后集市才开放。

examples.en: I asked to join the opening crew because my lectures did not start until noon.
examples.zh: 我的课中午才开始，所以我申请加入「开店班组」。

words.enDefinition: the workers responsible for finishing operations and closing a workplace at the end of the day

examples.en: The closing crew counted the remaining supplies before stacking the chairs near the storeroom.
examples.zh: 「收班班组」清点完剩余物资，才把椅子叠放在储藏室旁。

examples.en: Our closing crew left a brief note about an order still waiting for collection.
examples.zh: 我们的「收班班组」留了张简短的便条，说明还有一笔订单没人来取。

words.enDefinition: a worker who helps customers or visitors at a counter

examples.en: The counter attendant checked each receipt before handing over a bag from the shelf.
examples.zh: 「柜台服务员」先逐张核对收据，再从货架上取袋子交给顾客。

examples.en: I asked the counter attendant who could help students with a large equipment order.
examples.zh: 我问「柜台服务员」，谁能帮助要订大量器材的学生。

words.enDefinition: a person who oversees workers and service activity in the main working or customer area

examples.en: The floor supervisor moved the waiting area after the queue began blocking the main entrance.
examples.zh: 队伍开始挡住正门后，「现场主管」把等候区挪了位置。

examples.en: A floor supervisor checked that each new worker knew which station they were covering.
examples.zh: 一名「现场主管」确认每个新员工都知道自己负责哪个工位。

words.enDefinition: a door or access point intended for workers rather than customers or visitors

examples.en: The staff entrance was open when I arrived to help prepare for the morning market.
examples.zh: 我来帮忙筹备早市时，「员工入口」已经开了。

examples.en: We told the volunteers to meet by the staff entrance before their first shift.
examples.zh: 我们让志愿者第一班上岗前在「员工入口」集合。

words.enDefinition: a list of things to check or complete before opening a workplace

examples.en: The opening checklist included checking that no orders from the previous day were still on the shelf.
examples.zh: 「开店检查清单」要求检查货架上是否还有前一天的订单。

examples.en: We updated the opening checklist after the new display needed a separate power supply.
examples.zh: 新展示台需要单独接电，我们更新了「开店检查清单」。

words.enDefinition: a list of things to complete or verify when closing a business or finishing operations

examples.en: The closing checklist reminded us to record leftover stock and return the storeroom key.
examples.zh: 「收班检查清单」提醒我们记录剩余库存，并归还储藏室钥匙。

examples.en: I finished the closing checklist before leaving the stall with the last two volunteers.
examples.zh: 我完成了「收班检查清单」，和最后两名志愿者一起离开摊位。

words.enDefinition: the regular tasks workers carry out before a workplace opens for the day

examples.en: My opening duties included filling the display and checking which orders were ready for collection.
examples.zh: 我的「开店准备工作」包括补好展台上的货，确认哪些订单可以自取。

examples.en: We split the opening duties between three people so the counter could open on time.
examples.zh: 我们三个人分担了「开店准备工作」，柜台便能准时营业。

words.enDefinition: the regular tasks workers carry out to finish operations and close a workplace

examples.en: Our closing duties included packing the display and noting any repairs still waiting for collection.
examples.zh: 我们的「收班工作」包括收起展品，记下仍等着领取的维修件。

examples.en: I finished my closing duties before handing the keys to the supervisor at the entrance.
examples.zh: 我完成「收班工作」后，在入口把钥匙交给了主管。

words.enDefinition: chiefly British English for counting the cash and checking it against recorded sales at the end of a shift

examples.en: The manager completed the cash-up while I put away the signs beside the counter.
examples.zh: 我收起柜台旁的指示牌时，经理做完了「收班清点并核对现金」。

examples.en: We recorded a small difference during the cash-up and checked the earlier receipts together.
examples.zh: 「收班清点并核对现金」时，我们记下了一笔小差额，一起核对了早先的收据。

words.enDefinition: the amount of cash counted in a till when a shift or business day ends

examples.en: I entered the closing till count after the supervisor checked the notes beside the register.
examples.zh: 主管核对完收银机旁的记录后，我录入了「收班现金盘点金额」。

examples.en: The closing till count was lower than expected, so I asked the supervisor to check the receipts.
examples.zh: 「收班现金盘点金额」少于预期，我请主管核对收据。

words.enDefinition: a record of tasks, changes or incidents during a work shift

examples.en: The shift log showed that two orders had been moved to the evening collection shelf.
examples.zh: 「班次工作记录」显示，有两笔订单已经挪到了晚间自取货架。

examples.en: I entered the new opening time in the shift log before leaving for my seminar.
examples.zh: 我在去研讨课前，把新的开门时间填进了「班次工作记录」。

collocations: make an entry in the shift log

words.enDefinition: a short meeting before a shift to explain assignments, priorities and important changes

examples.en: The shift briefing covered new collection times before the first group of customers arrived.
examples.zh: 第一批顾客到来之前，「班前简报」讲了新的取货时间。

examples.en: Our shift briefing moved outside because the stall was still locked when everyone arrived.
examples.zh: 大家到齐时摊位还锁着，我们便把「班前简报」挪到外面开。

words.enDefinition: a report prepared at the end of a shift that summarises what happened or remains unfinished

examples.en: The end-of-shift report listed the orders we had completed and one repair still in progress.
examples.zh: 「班末报告」列出了我们完成的订单，还有一件仍在维修的物品。

examples.en: I checked the end-of-shift report before contacting the customer who had left a bag behind.
examples.zh: 联系落下包的顾客之前，我查了「班末报告」。

words.enDefinition: exchanging information between people who work at different times in the same operation

examples.en: The team improved cross-shift communication by keeping notes where both crews could read them.
examples.zh: 团队把记录放在两班人都能看到的地方，改进了「跨班次沟通」。

examples.en: We discussed cross-shift communication after the evening crew opened the wrong collection shelf twice.
examples.zh: 晚班两次开错自取货架后，我们讨论了怎么做好「跨班次沟通」。

words.enDefinition: to pass responsibility for an unfinished task to someone else who will continue it

examples.en: I needed to transfer an open task before leaving for my afternoon class downtown.
examples.zh: 去市区上下午的课前，我得「交接未完成的任务」。

examples.en: The coordinator asked how to transfer an open task without losing the notes attached to it.
examples.zh: 协调员问，怎样「交接未完成的任务」，同时保留附在任务里的记录。

collocations: transfer an open task to the next shift
choose to transfer an open task
transfer an open task to another worker

words.enDefinition: a schedule listing who is assigned to particular duties or times

examples.en: I checked the duty roster to find out who was looking after the display that afternoon.
examples.zh: 我看了「值班表」，查当天下午谁负责展示台。

examples.en: The new duty roster put a second person on collection during the lunch break.
examples.zh: 新「值班表」在午餐时段增加了一名负责取货的人。

words.enDefinition: a change to the order, timing or assignment of scheduled work shifts

examples.en: The manager sent a rota change after the student market extended its evening hours.
examples.zh: 学生集市延长晚间开放时间后，经理发出了「轮班表变更」。

examples.en: I confirmed the rota change with the coworker opening the counter the next morning.
examples.zh: 我和第二天上午负责开柜台的同事确认了「轮班表变更」。

collocations: notify staff about a rota change

words.enDefinition: to make the worker schedule available to the people who need to see it

examples.en: We agreed to publish the rota on Fridays so everyone could plan around weekend classes.
examples.zh: 我们商定每周五「发布轮班表」，让大家能腾出时间上周末的课。

examples.en: The manager waited to publish the rota until the fair's opening hours were confirmed.
examples.zh: 经理等展会开放时间确认后才「发布轮班表」。

collocations: publish the rota for next week
be ready to publish the rota

words.enDefinition: a schedule in which workers or teams regularly change their assigned shifts or duties

examples.en: The rotating schedule gave each worker a chance to do the more popular morning shift.
examples.zh: 「轮换排班」给每名员工机会轮到更受欢迎的早班。

examples.en: We switched to a rotating schedule after several people had classes on alternate Fridays.
examples.zh: 几个人隔周周五要上课，我们改用了「轮换排班」。

words.enDefinition: a schedule in which the assigned working hours or days stay the same on a regular basis

examples.en: My fixed schedule gave me the same two afternoons each week at the repair stand.
examples.zh: 我的「固定排班」是每周同样两个下午在维修摊工作。

examples.en: The owner offered a fixed schedule so I could plan my course commitments in advance.
examples.zh: 店主给我安排了「固定排班」，这样我可以提前安排课程事务。

words.enDefinition: work shifts that share a period when workers from both are on duty

examples.en: We used overlapping shifts so the morning crew could explain the work to the afternoon team.
examples.zh: 我们安排了「有重叠时段的班次」，让早班能向下午班说明手头工作。

examples.en: The schedule included overlapping shifts while the shop stayed open during the student fair.
examples.zh: 学生展会期间店面继续营业，排班表安排了「有重叠时段的班次」。

collocations: use overlapping shifts for a handover

words.enDefinition: start times deliberately spread out rather than scheduled for everyone at the same moment

examples.en: With staggered start times, we had enough workers when the campus gates opened at noon.
examples.zh: 用了「错峰上班时间」，校园大门中午开放时，我们的人手够用。

examples.en: We introduced staggered start times after finding that early deliveries needed only one worker.
examples.zh: 发现早间送货只要一名员工处理后，我们引入了「错峰上班时间」。

words.enDefinition: breaks taken by different workers at different times to maintain coverage

examples.en: The team took staggered breaks so the collection desk could remain open through lunch.
examples.zh: 团队采用「错开安排的休息时间」，让自取台在午餐时段继续开放。

examples.en: Our supervisor added staggered breaks to the schedule for the busiest day of the fair.
examples.zh: 主管给展会最忙的那天加了「错开安排的休息时间」。

words.enDefinition: the workers or arrangements needed to keep an operation working over the weekend

examples.en: We arranged weekend coverage because the art market was staying open until Sunday afternoon.
examples.zh: 艺术集市会开到周日下午，我们安排了「周末值班安排」。

examples.en: The team added a second worker for weekend coverage when Saturday orders began increasing.
examples.zh: 周六订单开始增加后，团队给「周末值班安排」多加了一人。

words.enDefinition: a shift during the later part of an operation's daily or regular working hours

examples.en: I chose the late shift at the book stall because my course ended after lunch.
examples.zh: 我的课午饭后才结束，所以选了书摊的「晚班」。

examples.en: I worked the late shift, so I collected the loan forms before the hall closed.
examples.zh: 我上「晚班」，就在大厅关闭之前收齐了借用表。

words.enDefinition: a scheduled shift that does not yet have a worker assigned to it

examples.en: I requested an open shift after my Friday seminar was moved to the following week.
examples.zh: 周五研讨课改到下周后，我申请了一个「待认领班次」。

examples.en: The coordinator added an open shift when the market announced that it would stay open later.
examples.zh: 集市宣布延长开放时间后，协调员添加了一个「待认领班次」。

words.enDefinition: to agree to work an additional shift that was not on your schedule

examples.en: I offered to pick up a shift between my lecture and the evening rehearsal.
examples.zh: 我提出在课后到晚间排练之间「接下一个额外班次」。

examples.en: My classmate could pick up a shift after checking that exams had not been moved.
examples.zh: 我的同学确认考试时间没改，可以「接下一个额外班次」。

collocations: offer to pick up a shift
ask to pick up a shift
pick up a shift at short notice

words.enDefinition: to ask whether another worker wants to take a shift assigned to you

examples.en: I chose to offer a shift to a coworker after the tutor moved our seminar.
examples.zh: 导师调整研讨课时间后，我选择向同事「提出转让一个班次」。

examples.en: The scheduling app lets workers offer a shift even when they do not need one back.
examples.zh: 排班应用允许员工「提出转让一个班次」，即使不需要别人换一个班给自己。

collocations: offer a shift to a colleague
learn how to offer a shift

words.enDefinition: a request for another worker to exchange an assigned shift with you

examples.en: The manager reviewed my shift trade request after both workers agreed to the new times.
examples.zh: 我们俩都同意新的时间后，经理审核了我的「换班请求」。

examples.en: I cancelled the shift trade request after my class was postponed until the next week.
examples.zh: 我的课推迟到下周，所以取消了「换班请求」。

collocations: respond to a shift trade request

words.enDefinition: arrangements to ensure that enough workers are available for a shift

examples.en: The coordinator confirmed shift coverage before inviting more customers to the afternoon sale on campus.
examples.zh: 协调员先确认「班次人员保障」，再邀请更多顾客参加校园下午的售卖活动。

examples.en: We needed shift coverage when the usual worker took time off for a class trip.
examples.zh: 平时值这个班的人请假参加班级出游，我们需要做好「班次人员保障」。

words.enDefinition: a period during which a person is free and can be scheduled for work

examples.en: I entered an availability window that started after my Tuesday afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 我录入的「可排班的时间范围」从周二下午下课后开始。

examples.en: The supervisor looked at each person's availability window before assigning the evening market shifts.
examples.zh: 主管分配晚间集市班次前，查看了每个人的「可排班的时间范围」。

words.enDefinition: days on which a person cannot work or take an assignment

examples.en: I shared my unavailable dates as soon as the university confirmed the exam timetable.
examples.zh: 学校一确认考试时间表，我就提交了自己「不能排班的日期」。

examples.en: The form asked us to list unavailable dates for the six weeks before the market.
examples.zh: 表格请我们列出集市开始前六周内「不能排班的日期」。

words.enDefinition: to state when you are generally free to accept assigned shifts or duties

examples.en: The app asks you to set your availability before the supervisor prepares next month's schedule.
examples.zh: 主管排下个月的班之前，应用会请你「设置可上班时间」。

examples.en: You can set your availability to start after class on the days you normally work.
examples.zh: 在平常上班的日子，你可以「设置可上班时间」为放学后开始。

collocations: set your availability in the app
ask how to set your availability

words.enDefinition: time that a worker is expected to work according to the schedule

examples.en: I checked my scheduled hours before agreeing to help with another stall during the fair.
examples.zh: 在答应展会期间去另一个摊位帮忙前，我查看了自己的「排定工时」。

examples.en: The schedule showed fewer scheduled hours once the shop reduced its opening times after exams.
examples.zh: 考试后店面缩短了开放时间，排班表上的「排定工时」也少了。

collocations: compare scheduled hours with actual hours

words.enDefinition: a missing record because a worker did not register the end of a shift

examples.en: I reported a missed clock-out after noticing that my Thursday shift had no end time.
examples.zh: 我发现周四那个班没记录结束时间，报了「漏打下班卡」。

examples.en: The supervisor corrected my missed clock-out after checking when the last customer had left.
examples.zh: 主管核实了最后一位顾客离开的时间，然后补录了我「漏打的下班卡」。

collocations: an entry for a missed clock-out

words.enDefinition: a rest period whose start or approximate timing is planned on a work schedule

examples.en: I took my scheduled break after the second cashier arrived to work at the counter.
examples.zh: 第二名收银员到柜台上岗后，我按「排定的休息时段」休息。

examples.en: The scheduled break moved by fifteen minutes when the workshop finished later than we expected.
examples.zh: 工作坊比预期结束得晚，「排定的休息时段」也挪了十五分钟。

words.enDefinition: staffing arrangements that keep work going when someone takes a break

examples.en: We planned break coverage so the equipment desk could answer questions throughout the lunch hour.
examples.zh: 我们做好了「休息时的替岗安排」，让器材台在午餐时段一直有人答疑。

examples.en: The shift lead checked break coverage before sending the packing team outside to eat lunch.
examples.zh: 值班组长先确认「休息时的替岗安排」，才让打包人员出去吃午饭。

words.enDefinition: the recorded time when a worker logs the start of work

examples.en: My clock-in time was five minutes after opening because the tablet took time to start.
examples.zh: 平板启动耽搁了一会儿，我的「上班打卡时间」是开门后五分钟。

examples.en: The supervisor checked my clock-in time after I noticed an error in the timesheet.
examples.zh: 我发现工时表有错后，主管核对了我的「上班打卡时间」。

words.enDefinition: the recorded time when a worker logs the end of work

examples.en: I checked my clock-out time before leaving the student centre after our evening shift.
examples.zh: 晚班结束后，我离开学生中心前查看了自己的「下班打卡时间」。

examples.en: The clock-out time was later than expected because we helped clear the display area.
examples.zh: 我们的「下班打卡时间」比预期晚，因为帮忙收拾了展示区。

words.enDefinition: a device or application used to record when employees begin and end work

examples.en: I used the time clock near the counter before putting on my work apron.
examples.zh: 我用柜台旁的「工时打卡系统」打完卡，才穿上工作围裙。

examples.en: The time clock showed a confirmation after I logged the end of my shift.
examples.zh: 我记录下班时间后，「工时打卡系统」显示了确认信息。

collocations: clock in at the time clock

words.enDefinition: a missing record because a worker did not register the start of a shift

examples.en: I reported a missed clock-in when the supervisor noticed a blank entry on the schedule.
examples.zh: 主管注意到那栏记录是空的，我报了「漏打上班卡」。

examples.en: The team lead explained how to correct a missed clock-in during our first training shift.
examples.zh: 值班组长在我们首班培训时解释了怎么补「漏打上班卡」。

words.enDefinition: a message or record confirming that someone has received a handover and its relevant information

examples.en: The coordinator waited for a handover acknowledgement before leaving the repair desk for the evening.
examples.zh: 协调员等收到「交接收悉确认」，才在晚上离开维修台。

examples.en: I sent a handover acknowledgement after finding both keys and the notes for tomorrow's stall.
examples.zh: 我找到两把钥匙和明天摊位用的记录后，发出了「交接收悉确认」。

words.enDefinition: confirmation that an employee's recorded hours have been reviewed and accepted

examples.en: The manager finished timesheet approval for the weekend team before the office closed on Monday.
examples.zh: 周一办公室关闭以前，经理完成了周末班组的「工时表审批」。

examples.en: I checked who was responsible for timesheet approval while our usual supervisor was away.
examples.zh: 平时的主管不在，我问了现在谁负责「工时表审批」。

words.enDefinition: the latest time at which workers are expected to send their timesheets for processing

examples.en: The coordinator moved the timesheet deadline ahead of the university's public holiday this month.
examples.zh: 协调员把「工时表提交截止时间」提前到学校本月的公休日前。

examples.en: I set a reminder for the timesheet deadline after missing the previous Friday's submission.
examples.zh: 上周五没交上之后，我给「工时表提交截止时间」设了提醒。

collocations: send a reminder about the timesheet deadline

words.enDefinition: the scheduled time when a work shift begins

examples.en: My shift start time changed because the repair stall was opening an hour earlier.
examples.zh: 维修摊提前一小时开门，我的「班次开始时间」也改了。

examples.en: We confirmed each person's shift start time before the student market opened that weekend.
examples.zh: 那个周末的学生集市开放前，我们确认了每个人的「班次开始时间」。

words.enDefinition: the scheduled time when a work shift is due to end

examples.en: I checked the shift end time before offering to help at the walled garden that evening.
examples.zh: 我先查看了「班次结束时间」，才提出当晚去围墙花园帮忙。

examples.en: The manager moved our shift end time after the last equipment collection was cancelled.
examples.zh: 最后一次设备领取取消后，经理调整了我们的「班次结束时间」。

words.enDefinition: a maximum number of items that may be actively worked on at one time

examples.en: Our work-in-progress limit meant we could start another repair only after finishing an existing one.
examples.zh: 根据「在办事项数量上限」，我们得先完成一项正在做的维修，才能开下一项。

examples.en: The team lowered its work-in-progress limit to stop too many orders reaching the counter together.
examples.zh: 团队调低了「在办事项数量上限」，免得太多订单同时送到柜台。

words.enDefinition: a labelled lane in a diagram or board used to group work by team, role or category

examples.en: Each swimlane on the flowchart showed which team was responsible for that part of the process.
examples.zh: 流程图里的每条「泳道」都标明了相应流程归哪个团队负责。

examples.en: We added a swimlane for items waiting for customers to collect after their repairs.
examples.zh: 我们加了一条「泳道」，放修好后等顾客领取的物品。

collocations: move a card to another swimlane

words.enDefinition: the person responsible for ensuring that a specific task is completed

examples.en: The task owner checked with both shifts before changing the collection shelf labels that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午，「任务负责人」先和两班人确认，再换自取货架的标签。

examples.en: Each card listed the task owner and the time when the work was due.
examples.zh: 每张卡片列出了「任务负责人」和任务的截止时间。

words.enDefinition: a table that identifies what role each person or group has for a set of tasks

examples.en: The responsibility matrix showed who should approve repairs and who should contact each customer.
examples.zh: 「职责分配矩阵」标明了谁批准维修、谁联系各位顾客。

examples.en: We drew a simple responsibility matrix after two teams both tried to order new materials.
examples.zh: 两支团队都想订购新材料后，我们画了一份简单的「职责分配矩阵」。

words.enDefinition: to complete work that has accumulated and is still waiting to be processed

examples.en: We needed two quiet afternoons to clear the backlog before accepting new repair orders.
examples.zh: 接新维修订单前，我们得用两个空闲的下午「清理积压事项」。

examples.en: The team stayed an extra hour to clear the backlog of equipment labels that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午团队多留了一小时，「清理积压的器材标签制作任务」。

words.zhGloss: 把一项任务留到下一轮
words.enDefinition: to leave a task unfinished and move it into the next working period
acceptedZhAnswers: 把一项任务留到下一轮

examples.en: The shift lead decided to carry over a task that needed the spare keys.
examples.zh: 值班组长决定「把一项任务留到下一轮」，因为这项任务得用备用钥匙。

examples.en: I added a note when I had to carry over a task until Monday morning.
examples.zh: 我不得不「把一项任务留到下一轮」、等周一早上再做，所以加了条备注。

collocations: carry over a task to the next shift
decide to carry over a task
carry over a task if necessary

words.enDefinition: a list of checks or tasks for switching a workstation from one job to another

examples.en: We used a changeover checklist before switching the printer from signs to small price labels.
examples.zh: 把打印机从印指示牌切换为印小价签前，我们用了「切换准备清单」。

examples.en: The changeover checklist reminded me to put away the blocks from the previous printing job.
examples.zh: 「切换准备清单」提醒我收好上一项印刷工作用过的印版。

words.enDefinition: to transfer an already assigned task to a different person or team

examples.en: We had to reassign a task when the worker responsible for labelling left early.
examples.zh: 负责贴标签的员工早退了，我们得「重新指派任务」。

examples.en: The supervisor chose to reassign a task that was holding up work at the counter.
examples.zh: 主管选择「重新指派任务」，调整那项耽搁柜台工作的任务。

collocations: reassign a task to another worker

words.enDefinition: the act of assigning work or the particular task allocated to a person

examples.en: The task assignment gave me responsibility for checking delivery times during the student market.
examples.zh: 「任务指派」让我负责在学生集市期间核对送货时间。

examples.en: We reviewed the task assignment after noticing that two people were checking the same boxes.
examples.zh: 发现两个人在检查同一批箱子后，我们重新查看了「任务指派」。

words.enDefinition: the current stage of a task, such as waiting, in progress or complete

examples.en: I updated the task status once the customer had collected the last repaired item.
examples.zh: 顾客取走最后一件修好的物品后，我更新了「任务状态」。

examples.en: The afternoon shift checked each task status before deciding whether to open another station.
examples.zh: 下午班在决定要不要多开一个工位之前，检查了每个「任务状态」。

words.enDefinition: work that must be completed promptly because a delay would cause significant problems

examples.en: Printing the last labels was a time-critical task before the boxes could leave on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五箱子发走前，印好最后一批标签是个「时限紧迫的任务」。

examples.en: The supervisor moved a second worker onto the time-critical task just before the afternoon break.
examples.zh: 下午休息前，主管又加了一人去做「时限紧迫的任务」。

words.enDefinition: to mark a task on a list to show it has been completed

examples.en: I waited to check off a task until the printed copies were on the counter.
examples.zh: 纸质副本放到了柜台上，我才「勾选任务为已完成」。

examples.en: The checklist showed when to check off a task such as counting the remaining supplies.
examples.zh: 检查清单说明了清点剩余物资之类的工作何时可以「勾选为已完成」。

collocations: check off a task on the list
remember to check off a task
check off a task after completing it

words.enDefinition: a way of working that can be followed again under similar conditions

examples.en: We wanted a repeatable process that worked even when a different volunteer opened the stall.
examples.zh: 我们想要一套「可重复执行的流程」，换一个志愿者开摊也能照做。

examples.en: The trainer turned the preparation notes into a repeatable process for the whole team.
examples.zh: 培训员把准备记录整理成整个班组都能使用的「可重复执行的流程」。

words.enDefinition: a written or established procedure describing how to carry out a recurring operation consistently

examples.en: The repair shop wrote a standard operating procedure for receiving equipment from customers at the counter.
examples.zh: 维修店给在柜台接收顾客器材制定了一份「标准操作规程」。

examples.en: We followed the standard operating procedure while checking labelled orders before opening the collection shelf.
examples.zh: 打开自取货架前，我们依照「标准操作规程」核对了贴好标签的订单。

words.enDefinition: a document or set of directions explaining how to perform a specific work task

examples.en: The work instruction showed which label went on each kind of returned item in the shop.
examples.zh: 「作业指导书」说明了店里不同种类的退回品该贴哪种标签。

examples.en: We added a photograph to the work instruction for setting up the second display shelf.
examples.zh: 我们在搭建第二个展示架的「作业指导书」中加了一张照片。

words.enDefinition: a quick reference that helps a worker carry out a particular task while doing it

examples.en: The new cashier kept a small job aid beside the register to check uncommon payment options.
examples.zh: 新收银员把一份小小的「岗位操作提示」放在收银机旁，用来查看不常见的支付选项。

examples.en: I drew a simple job aid showing where to put equipment ready for pickup.
examples.zh: 我画了一张简单的「岗位操作提示」，标明可以领取的设备该放哪里。

words.enDefinition: the person responsible for maintaining and updating an established procedure

examples.en: The procedure owner updated the collection instructions after the shop moved to another building.
examples.zh: 店面搬到另一栋楼后，「流程负责人」更新了取货说明。

examples.en: We asked the procedure owner whether the same checklist applied to the weekend stall.
examples.zh: 我们问「流程负责人」，周末摊位是不是也用这份检查清单。

words.enDefinition: a visual representation of the steps, decisions and handoffs involved in completing a process

examples.en: The process map showed where a customer order passed from the counter to packing.
examples.zh: 「流程图」标出了顾客订单从柜台转到打包环节的位置。

examples.en: We updated the process map after moving the final inspection to the collection desk.
examples.zh: 我们把最后检查挪到自取台后，更新了「流程图」。

words.enDefinition: the stage that limits how quickly work can pass through an entire process

examples.en: Packing became a process bottleneck when three stalls sent orders to one worker at once.
examples.zh: 三个摊位同时把订单交给一名员工，打包成了「流程瓶颈」。

examples.en: We looked for a process bottleneck after noticing a long wait between checkout and pickup.
examples.zh: 发现结账后到取货前要等很久，我们开始找「流程瓶颈」。

words.enDefinition: the elapsed time to complete one repeated unit of work or operation

examples.en: We measured cycle time for printing one badge so we could plan our staffing.
examples.zh: 我们测量了印一枚徽章的「周期时间」，以便安排人手。

examples.en: The cycle time fell after we moved frequently used supplies closer to the table.
examples.zh: 常用物资移到桌边之后，「周期时间」缩短了。

words.enDefinition: the amount of work or number of units a process completes during a given time

examples.en: The stall's throughput increased after two workers began packing orders at separate tables.
examples.zh: 两名员工分桌打包后，摊位的「单位时间处理量」提高了。

examples.en: We measured throughput in repaired items per hour during the first afternoon of the fair.
examples.zh: 展会第一个下午，我们按每小时修好的物品数衡量「单位时间处理量」。

words.enDefinition: the maximum amount of work an operation can handle in a day under given conditions

examples.en: Our daily capacity fell once two repair benches were needed for a different event.
examples.zh: 两张维修台被调去办另一场活动，我们的「日处理能力」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated the daily capacity before setting a limit on bookings for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们先计算「日处理能力」，再给工作坊设定预约上限。

words.enDefinition: the amount of work a particular station can complete in a set time under given conditions

examples.en: We compared workstation capacity at the two benches before assigning the afternoon repair orders.
examples.zh: 分派下午的维修订单前，我们比较了两张工作台的「工位处理能力」。

examples.en: The supervisor checked workstation capacity when the team added another printer to the label desk.
examples.zh: 团队为标签台增添一台打印机时，主管查看了「工位处理能力」。

words.enDefinition: time when a worker or piece of equipment is available but is not doing its intended work

examples.en: We recorded idle time while the team waited for the materials to reach the workshop.
examples.zh: 团队等材料送到工作室时，我们记录了「闲置时间」。

examples.en: The printer's idle time fell after we put all the label requests in one place.
examples.zh: 标签打印需求集中到一起以后，打印机的「闲置时间」减少了。

words.enDefinition: time needed to prepare equipment or a working area before a task can begin

examples.en: We allowed extra setup time because our display tables had to be brought from another hall.
examples.zh: 展示桌需要从另一座厅搬来，我们多留了些「准备时间」。

examples.en: The new racks shortened setup time before each afternoon collection at the repair desk.
examples.zh: 维修台每天下午开放取货前，新货架缩短了「准备时间」。

words.enDefinition: time needed to switch a process, station or machine from one job or product to another

examples.en: We reduced changeover time by keeping both sizes of paper beside the same printer.
examples.zh: 我们把两种尺寸的纸都放在同一台打印机旁，缩短了「切换准备时间」。

examples.en: The changeover time between two different badge sizes was longer than one complete printing cycle.
examples.zh: 两种徽章尺寸的「切换准备时间」比一个完整的打印周期还长。

words.enDefinition: a record of periods when equipment or an operation could not be used as planned

examples.en: The downtime log showed how long the label printer was unavailable during the morning shift.
examples.zh: 「停工记录」显示，标签打印机在早班期间有多久不能用。

examples.en: Our supervisor checked the downtime log before deciding which equipment needed attention this week.
examples.zh: 主管先查看「停工记录」，再决定本周哪些设备需要处理。

words.enDefinition: the share of available staff time spent on the work an organisation counts as productive

examples.en: We measured staff utilisation during the fair to see whether the repair bench needed another worker.
examples.zh: 展会期间我们统计了「人员工时利用率」，看看维修台是否需要再加一名员工。

examples.en: The student enterprise reviewed staff utilisation before changing the hours at its two service desks.
examples.zh: 学生企业在改动两处服务台的工作时间之前，查看了「人员工时利用率」。

words.enDefinition: a list of jobs awaiting processing, often in an order that determines what is done next

examples.en: My work queue contained three label requests and a repair form when I started the shift.
examples.zh: 我开始上班时，「待处理工作队列」里有三项标签请求和一张维修单。

examples.en: The team moved rush orders to the front of the work queue before the post office closed.
examples.zh: 邮局关门前，团队把加急订单调到了「待处理工作队列」最前面。

collocations: add a job to the work queue

words.enDefinition: the rule an operation uses to decide which waiting person or job is served next

examples.en: We changed the queue discipline so booked repairs were handled before walk-in requests.
examples.zh: 我们调整了「排队处理规则」，让预约维修先于现场申请处理。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the queue discipline would deal with people who had already booked.
examples.zh: 导师问，「排队处理规则」会怎么处理那些已经预约的人。

words.enDefinition: the average time the worker takes to handle an interaction, often including related work after it

examples.en: The team tracked average handle time for repair questions at the student enterprise's service desk.
examples.zh: 团队统计了学生企业服务台回答维修问题的「平均处理时长」。

examples.en: Our average handle time fell after the team made the booking records easier to find.
examples.zh: 团队让预约记录更好找之后，「平均处理时长」缩短了。

words.enDefinition: a prediction of how long someone or something will wait before being served or processed

examples.en: The desk displayed a wait time estimate after the number of people needing repairs doubled.
examples.zh: 需要维修的人翻了一倍后，服务台显示了「预计等候时长」。

examples.en: The coordinator updated the wait time estimate when the second worker returned from the break.
examples.zh: 第二名员工休息回来后，协调员更新了「预计等候时长」。

words.enDefinition: extra capacity held available so an operation can absorb greater demand or interruptions

examples.en: We kept a capacity buffer in case more students arrived than the workshop bookings suggested.
examples.zh: 我们保留了「备用处理能力」，以防来的人比工作坊预约人数多。

examples.en: A capacity buffer let the repair desk take two urgent jobs without delaying the afternoon orders.
examples.zh: 有了「备用处理能力」，维修台接两件加急活也不耽误下午的订单。

words.enDefinition: the way an organisation handles cases that fall outside its normal procedure

examples.en: The supervisor taught exception handling for orders with missing names during our first training session.
examples.zh: 首次培训时，主管以缺少姓名的订单为例，讲解了「例外情况处理」。

examples.en: We reviewed exception handling after discovering that several visiting societies had no local contact number.
examples.zh: 发现几个来访社团没有本地联系电话后，我们重新检查了「例外情况处理」流程。

words.enDefinition: to mark a particular matter as needing further attention or action later

examples.en: If a booking still looked uncertain, we had to flag it for follow-up before closing.
examples.zh: 如果预约还有疑问，我们得在关门前「将这件事标记待跟进」。

examples.en: I couldn't match the form to an order, so I had to flag it for follow-up.
examples.zh: 我找不到与那张表对应的订单，只好「将这件事标记待跟进」。

collocations: flag it for follow-up by the next shift
flag it for follow-up before closing

words.enDefinition: instruction or guided practice provided during a person's assigned work hours

examples.en: I received on-shift training at the repair stall when orders were slow on Tuesday morning.
examples.zh: 周二上午订单少，我在维修摊参加了「当班培训」。

examples.en: The supervisor scheduled on-shift training for new staff before the last week of the term.
examples.zh: 主管在学期最后一周前给新员工安排了「当班培训」。

words.enDefinition: to teach workers to carry out tasks in more than one role or area

examples.en: We wanted to cross-train staff so the stall could stay open if someone was absent.
examples.zh: 我们想「给员工做跨岗位培训」，这样有人缺勤时摊位也能营业。

examples.en: The owner agreed to cross-train staff in order collection and the preparation of stock labels.
examples.zh: 店主同意「给员工做跨岗位培训」，涵盖自取和制作库存标签。

words.enDefinition: an explanation that shows a worker or trainee how to carry out a particular task

examples.en: The task demonstration showed new staff how to compare each label with the order form.
examples.zh: 「工作任务示范」给新员工展示了怎么把每张标签和订单表核对。

examples.en: I repeated the task demonstration because the workers on the later shift had missed it.
examples.zh: 晚班的人没看到，我又做了一次「工作任务示范」。

words.enDefinition: a colleague paired with a new worker to help them learn tasks and settle in

examples.en: My training buddy showed me where to record orders that needed to be collected later.
examples.zh: 「培训搭档」给我指了该在哪里记录稍后来取的订单。

examples.en: We assigned every new volunteer a training buddy for the first two shifts that month.
examples.zh: 我们给当月每位新志愿者在头两个班次安排了「培训搭档」。

words.enDefinition: a list of topics or tasks that should be covered or verified during training

examples.en: I used the training checklist to make sure we had practised each step twice together.
examples.zh: 我用「培训检查清单」确认我们每个步骤都一起练过两次。

examples.en: The coordinator added a new returns task to the training checklist for student volunteers.
examples.zh: 协调员在学生志愿者的「培训检查清单」上加了一项新的归还任务。

words.enDefinition: formal confirmation that someone is ready to perform an assigned task without direct supervision

examples.en: The student received sign-off to work independently after completing two shifts with an experienced partner.
examples.zh: 和一位有经验的搭档完成两个班次后，这名学生获得「独立上岗批准」。

examples.en: I asked when workers could get sign-off to work independently at the new equipment desk.
examples.zh: 我问，新器材台的员工什么时候能获得「独立上岗批准」。

words.enDefinition: verification in which two people check something, often to catch a mistake one person might miss

examples.en: We did a two-person check on the order total before giving the boxes to the customer.
examples.zh: 把箱子交给顾客之前，我们对订单总计做了「双人核查」。

examples.en: The checklist required a two-person check whenever the spare keys changed hands during a busy shift.
examples.zh: 清单规定，繁忙班次内每次交接备用钥匙都要「双人核查」。

words.enDefinition: a check of selected examples or a check made at an unannounced time

examples.en: The supervisor did a spot check on five labels from the afternoon batch of orders.
examples.zh: 主管「抽查」了下午这批订单的五张标签。

examples.en: A spot check revealed that two items had been placed on the wrong collection shelf.
examples.zh: 一次「抽查」发现，两件物品被放到了错误的自取架上。

words.enDefinition: a situation in which some people or stations have substantially more work than others

examples.en: The supervisor noticed a workload imbalance when all the afternoon orders went to one bench.
examples.zh: 下午订单全都去了同一张工作台，主管发现「工作量分配不均」。

examples.en: We changed the labels to reduce a workload imbalance between the two service desks.
examples.zh: 我们调整了标签，以缓解两处服务台之间的「工作量分配不均」。

words.zhGloss: 把某人从一项任务上调开
words.enDefinition: to remove a person from a task, often so they can work on something more urgent
acceptedZhAnswers: 把某人从一项任务上调开

examples.en: We had to pull someone off a task to help with the checkout queue.
examples.zh: 我们得「把某人从一项任务上调开」，去帮忙处理结账队伍。

examples.en: The lead checked whether she could pull someone off a task without delaying the repair orders.
examples.zh: 负责人先确认，是否能「把某人从一项任务上调开」而不耽误维修订单。

collocations: pull someone off a task temporarily
decide to pull someone off a task
pull someone off a task to help elsewhere

words.enDefinition: to become involved and offer help when a person or team needs extra support

examples.en: I offered to step in to help when the queue reached the edge of the courtyard.
examples.zh: 队伍排到庭院边缘时，我主动提出「临时出面帮忙」。

examples.en: The owner asked a worker from the next stall to step in to help briefly.
examples.zh: 店主请隔壁摊位的一名员工「临时出面帮忙」。

collocations: offer to step in to help
ask someone to step in to help
be willing to step in to help

words.enDefinition: a brief conversation during a shift to see how work is progressing and what help is needed

examples.en: We held a mid-shift check-in after lunch to see which orders could be finished that day.
examples.zh: 午饭后我们做了次「班中碰头会」，看看哪些订单当天能做完。

examples.en: The mid-shift check-in let us move someone to the service desk before the queue grew.
examples.zh: 「班中碰头会」让我们在排队的人变多前调了一人去服务台。

words.enDefinition: to work at a counter for a time so the usual worker can do something else

examples.en: I offered to cover the counter while my coworker collected boxes from the storeroom downstairs.
examples.zh: 同事去楼下储藏室拿箱子时，我主动提出「代为照看柜台」。

examples.en: We asked a trained volunteer to cover the counter until the afternoon cashier came back.
examples.zh: 我们请一名受过培训的志愿者「代为照看柜台」，等下午班收银员回来。

collocations: cover the counter for ten minutes
ask someone to cover the counter
cover the counter during a break

words.enDefinition: to operate the cash register and handle transactions during a period of work

examples.en: I learned to work the register at the market before helping with the afternoon shift.
examples.zh: 去下午班帮忙之前，我先学了怎么在集市上「负责收银」。

examples.en: The supervisor asked who could work the register while the usual cashier took a break.
examples.zh: 主管问，平时的收银员休息时谁能「负责收银」。

collocations: train someone to work the register

words.enDefinition: cash placed in a till at the start of a shift so workers can give change

examples.en: We checked the register float before opening the stall to customers on Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 周六上午摊位开门接待顾客前，我们核了「收银找零备用金」。

examples.en: The closing report showed how much register float the next shift would receive for change.
examples.zh: 收班报告写了下一班会收到多少「收银找零备用金」。

words.enDefinition: a thorough clean of a work area after an activity or shift has finished

examples.en: Our usual clean-down took longer because the last workshop used every table in the room.
examples.zh: 最后一场工作坊用了屋里所有桌子，例行的「营业后的清洁收拾」花了更长时间。

examples.en: We agreed who would do the clean-down before the morning crew arrived to set up.
examples.zh: 我们商定了早班来布置前，由谁负责「营业后的清洁收拾」。

words.zhGloss: 把工位恢复到就绪状态
words.enDefinition: to put equipment and materials back in place so a station is ready for its next use
acceptedZhAnswers: 把工位恢复到就绪状态

examples.en: I stayed to reset the station after the final customer collected a repaired light.
examples.zh: 最后一位顾客取走修好的灯后，我留下来「把工位恢复到就绪状态」。

examples.en: Our team had to reset the station before using the table for a different workshop.
examples.zh: 桌子用于另一场工作坊之前，我们团队得「把工位恢复到就绪状态」。

collocations: reset the station after each job

words.enDefinition: to replace used supplies and restore the amount needed at a work station

examples.en: We stopped to replenish the station with labels after processing the last group of returns.
examples.zh: 处理完上一批退回的物品，我们停下来「给工位补齐标签」。

examples.en: The duty manager asked where to find more supplies to replenish the station before lunch.
examples.zh: 值班经理问午饭前去哪儿找更多物资，好「给工位补齐物资」。

words.enDefinition: an absence reported so close to a scheduled shift that there is little time to adjust

examples.en: We dealt with a short-notice absence by moving someone to the front desk for lunch.
examples.zh: 有人「临时缺勤」，我们调了一人午餐时段去前台顶岗。

examples.en: The rota showed who to call if a short-notice absence left the stall without cover.
examples.zh: 排班表写了如果有人「临时缺勤」、摊位没人顶班，该给谁打电话。

words.enDefinition: regularly moving workers between tasks so they share different duties

examples.en: The supervisor introduced task rotation so everyone could practise both packing and helping at the counter.
examples.zh: 主管引入了「任务轮换」，让每个人都能练习打包和柜台服务。

examples.en: We used task rotation during the market instead of leaving one worker on labels all day.
examples.zh: 集市期间我们实行「任务轮换」，没有让一名员工整天贴标签。

words.enDefinition: a check that people, equipment or supplies are prepared before work begins

examples.en: We completed a readiness check before letting the first group into the equipment workshop.
examples.zh: 我们做完了「就绪确认」，才让第一组进器材工作坊。

examples.en: The shift lead held a readiness check while the afternoon crew set out new labels.
examples.zh: 下午班摆出新标签时，值班组长做了「就绪确认」。

words.enDefinition: the ability to keep essential work going when people, schedules or conditions change unexpectedly

examples.en: Keeping spare tools nearby helped maintain operational continuity during the busy university fair.
examples.zh: 校园展会期间，店里在近处备了一套工具，以维持「运营连续性」。

examples.en: The new roster helped maintain operational continuity while two supervisors attended training on different days.
examples.zh: 两名主管分不同日子参加培训，新排班表帮助维持了「运营连续性」。
